trajectory_summary: The call is dominated by several minutes of confused cross-talk where a third party appears to read out unrelated utility bill figures while the rep is trying to run basic verify questions, and the rep never resolves what that cross-talk actually was. Despite the chaos, the rep held the verify sequence together, caught a mapping inconsistency, and closed on a specific day and time. The outcome is a real booked appointment but built on a verify pass that is only partially trustworthy given how noisy the middle of the call was.

observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep and customer land on a specific day (Monday) and time (4:30, after the customer specified after 4:00), which meets the booked bar; however the co-owner son identified on the title was never confirmed for the appointment.

primary_coaching_focus.why: Several minutes of the call are consumed by numbers and confirmations that don't map cleanly to Ion's verify questions, and the rep never stops to clarify whose bill or account this is — the closer will inherit a qualification record with unexplained noise in it.

key_moments.stewart_read: This appears to be a third party in the house reading out a completely different bill (possibly a receipt or a different utility) rather than the customer's electric bill. The rep never clarifies whose numbers these are or what bill they came from.
